rounds.text: Mazda Ltd trades at a modest P/E ratio of 13.6 [E1] and exhibits superior capital efficiency compared to sector benchmarks, boasting an ROE of 14.58% and an ROCE of 19.76% [E9, E10]. Growth acceleration is already visible with trailing twelve-month sales compounding at 37% and profits surging by 51% [E17, E21], while quarterly operating margins expanded significantly by 6 percentage points year-over-year in September 2026 [E31]. The company maintains a pristine balance sheet with zero borrowings and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E37, E38], supported by a healthy dividend payout of 26.2% [E60] and a robust order book standing at approximately ₹115 to ₹116 crores [E86]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of ₹476 per share, offering a substantial margin of safety [E44, E45], backed by positive institutional money flow [E43] and a high relative-strength rating of 91 [E50]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at ₹-19 Cr in March 2026, leading to a weak cash conversion ratio of -0.68x [E34, E35].

The company exhibits a pronounced stagnation in top and bottom-line expansion over medium-term horizons, registering a compounded sales growth of merely 3% [E16] and profit growth of just 1% [E3] over the last three years. This tepid performance is further reflected in shareholder returns, with the compounded share price growth dropping to -1% over the same three-year period [E24]. Underlying operational health shows acute stress, evidenced by a deeply negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr for March 2026, leading to a distressed cash conversion ratio of -0.68x [E34, E35, E36]. Working capital requirements have also deteriorated significantly, with debtor days ballooning from 77.4 to 102 days and total working capital days surging from 125 to 187 days [E63, E64]. Furthermore, management has explicitly acknowledged that intense competition from indigenous and overseas manufacturers has sparked a price war, keeping operating margins under persistent pressure [E84]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative balance sheet with zero borrowings [E37] and trades at a P/E of 13.6x [E1].

Conceded: compounded sales growth over 3 years is 3% [E16], profit growth is 1% [E20], and share price growth is -1% over the same three-year window [E24]. However, focusing solely on a three-year snapshot ignores the dramatic acceleration in the trailing twelve months, where sales surged 37% [E17] and profits jumped 51% [E21]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows were negative at Rs -19 Cr and Rs -23 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E35, E36], but this must be balanced against a pristine, completely debt-free balance sheet with zero borrowings [E37, E38] that provides immense financial resilience. While debtor and working capital days have indeed lengthened [E63, E64], quarterly operating margins expanded by 6 percentage points year-over-year to 27% in September 2026 [E31], proving pricing power despite intense competition. Furthermore, the company commands a substantial order book of roughly 115 to 116 crores [E86], and management expects fiscal year performance to match or exceed the preceding year [E75], while trading at an attractive P/E of 13.6x [E1] that sits well below sector benchmarks [E6].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales surged 37% and profits jumped 51% [E17, E21], and quarterly operating margin expanded by 6 percentage points to 27% in September 2026 [E31]. However, framing this as a permanent acceleration ignores the structural multi-year stagnation where 3-year sales growth crawled at 3% and profit growth at 1% [E16, E20], leaving a 3-year share price return at -1% [E24]. Dismissing negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr in March 2026 as a minor bludgeon ignores the severe cash conversion collapse to -0.68x [E34, E35, E36]. While the balance sheet is technically debt-free [E37], working capital bloat has worsened dangerously as debtor days stretched from 77.4 to 102 days and overall working capital days expanded from 125 to 187 days [E63, E64]. Furthermore, the order book of Rs 115 to 116 crores [E86] remains virtually flat compared to prior periods [E87], confirming that top-line momentum lacks continuous backlog renewal. Finally, while P/E sits at 13.6x [E1], management itself concedes that fierce price wars from intense indigenous and overseas competition are keeping margins under constant pressure [E84].

Conceded: 3-year sales and profit growth slowed to 3% and 1% respectively [E16, E20], and the 3-year share price return registered -1% [E24]. Conceded: operating cash flow hit Rs -19 Cr alongside free cash flow of Rs -23 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], and debtor days expanded to 102 [E63]. However, the bear's fixation on past stagnation completely ignores the explosive recent acceleration where trailing twelve-month sales surged 37% and profits jumped 51% [E17, E21]. This exceptional operational velocity is further underlined by quarterly operating margins expanding by 6 percentage points to reach 27% in September 2026 [E31]. Furthermore, pointing to flat order books ignores that the company sits on Rs 115 to 116 crores in active orders on hand [E86], while maintaining a pristine zero-debt balance sheet that provides absolute financial resilience against any competitive pressure [E37]. Finally, the current valuation remains highly attractive, trading at a P/E of just 13.6x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 9.32x compared to the sector benchmark of 12.25x [E11], while generating superior ROCE of 19.76% against the sector benchmark of 12.91% [E10].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales surged 37% and profits jumped 51% [E17, E21], and quarterly operating margin reached 27% in September 2026 [E31]. However, citing this explosive recent acceleration ignores the structural stagnation of a 3-year sales growth of 3% and profit growth of 1% [E16, E20], alongside a negative 3-year share price return of -1% [E24]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on a Rs 115 to 116 crore order book [E86] masks the company's admission that current order booking is merely in the same vicinity as the prior year, with management explicitly noting a slowdown in the speed of incoming inquiries and projects [E77, E87]. Conceded: the balance sheet shows zero debt [E37], but this financial cushion does nothing to offset the severe operational drain that produced negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 crores and negative free cash flow of Rs -23 crores in March 2026 [E35, E36]. Finally, while the bull highlights a P/E of 13.6x [E1], it glosses over the alarming deterioration in working capital where debtor days expanded to 102 and working capital days blew out to 187 days [E63, E64].

evidence.fact: Management noted a certain degree of slowness or return in the speed of inquiries and incoming projects for the future.

evidence.fact: The export market tends to be very volatile, giving constant unpredictability in dollar price fluctuations and access to banking systems in African countries.
evidence.quote: The export market has been volatile. I think there was a question about the outlook for exports- the US and UK has picked up, which was substantially lower last year, but then again, we have instances like Sudan where there has been unrest and one of our largest customers in Sudan. So, the export market tends to be very volatile, giving us constant unpredictability, whether it is in dollar, price fluctuations, whether it is in African countries being able to access their dollar or the banking system etc., etc.

evidence.fact: Competition from indigenous and overseas manufacturers is increasing intensely, creating a price war and keeping margins under pressure.

Margins are under pressure always
